knowledge.text: In the current search-and-transform edit, the Candidate still failed two tasks that its verified Parent completed after the Candidate opened the fridge early and then cycled among previously inspected locations. On train:0021 (P2 success in 29 steps vs Q2 step_limit at 50), Q2 opened the fridge and found no bread there (Q2:5-Q2:6), then repeatedly returned to fridge 1, countertop 1/2, and cabinets; unlike P2, which took bread 1 from countertop 3 (P2:24-P2:25), Q2's logged actions do not include countertop 3. On train:0023 (P4 success in 15 vs Q4 step_limit at 50), Q4 opened the fridge early (Q4:2-Q4:3) but reached diningtable 1 only at Q4:48, took bread at Q4:49, and ended at step 50 before cooling or delivering. These Parent-success/Candidate-failure regressions arose under a bundled search edit, so they do not by themselves isolate which added search clause caused the divergence.

Even when the new fridge-priority guidance was followed, it did not prevent repeated travel or produce success when the goal object was not in the fridge. In train:0025 (P6/Q6) and train:0026 (P7/Q7), both sides ended at the 50-step limit. The Candidate opened the fridge early (Q6:7-Q6:8; Q7:4-Q7:5) but later returned repeatedly to the already-opened fridge (Q6:13, Q6:21, Q6:33, Q6:38; Q7:10, Q7:27, Q7:39, Q7:48). Thus the fridge clause was applicable and evidently followed, but it yielded no target acquisition or whole-task benefit in these observations.

In train:0027 (P8 success in 13 steps vs Q8 success in 43), the new search emphasis on unopened closed containers/fridge was associated with a large success-preserving step inflation: the Parent went from countertop 1 to diningtable 1 and took apple 1 at P8:3, whereas the Candidate went from countertop 1 to the unopened fridge (Q8:2-Q8:3), then searched cabinets/shelf and revisited fridge 1/countertop 1 repeatedly before taking apple 1 from diningtable 1 at Q8:39. It still finished after heating the held apple at the microwave (Q8:41) and delivering it (Q8:43). The Candidate's initial choice of the fridge rather than the unobserved target-bearing open surface is consistent with, but not uniquely determined by, the added closed-container preference.

In train:0029 (P10 step_limit at 50 vs Q10 success in 9), the Candidate continued to the next not-yet-observed open surface after countertop 1 and countertop 2: it checked countertop 3, took mug 4 (Q10:3-Q10:4), heated mug 4 while holding it at the microwave (Q10:6-Q10:7), and delivered it to the coffeemachine (Q10:9). The Parent turned to cabinets after countertop 2 and never found a mug. This Parent-failure/Candidate-success contrast is consistent with the edited unvisited-location preference, but the initial route choice and the direct-transform shortcut both contribute, so the benefit is not uniquely attributable to one clause.

The added direct-transform instruction was adhered to in Candidate runs and produced local step savings in pairs where the objects were otherwise reached. On train:0022 (P3 success in 8 vs Q3 success in 6), the Parent opened the fridge before later cooling the bread (P3:1-P3:6), while the Candidate cooled the held bread directly at the closed fridge (Q3:4) and delivered it (Q3:6). On train:0028 (P9 success in 15 vs Q9 success in 10), the Parent moved the egg into the microwave, toggled open/close/open/close (P9:7-P9:12), then took it out and heated it (P9:13), while the Candidate heated the held egg directly at the closed microwave (Q9:8). The Candidate also used direct transforms in Q1:5, Q5:27, Q8:41 and Q10:7, and in each successful Candidate run the transform preceded the final move.

Across the current batch, the Candidate preserved immediate pickup and direct post-transform delivery when it encountered the goal object: examples include Q1:3 taking spoon 2 from the first countertop that contained it, Q3:2 taking bread 1, Q5:25 taking pan 1, Q8:39 taking apple 1, Q9:6 taking egg 1, and Q10:4 taking mug 4. Each successful Candidate run moved the transformed object to the target immediately after the transform (Q1:7, Q3:6, Q5:29, Q8:43, Q9:10, Q10:9). Even in the failing Q4 run, it took bread 1 immediately upon finding it (Q4:49), but ran out of steps before transforming or delivering, so no successful Candidate run delivered an untransformed object.
